reviews.review:
My pals and I have played this off and on since the Demo, and overall I really like this game. It's a little clunkier than other games in it's genre, but that's what makes a good build feel so good. This game doesn't want you wasting any time, and it expects you to move fast and get as many items and upgrades as you can. It also expects you to grind, which is fun if you join a lobby or convince some pals to buy the game.

That being said, I personally felt like The Stabbening should have been when they released it as early access. The game has a lot of potential to grow, but it felt exactly like the demo until that update. I'd like to see more characters; there's a lot they could do with the fantasy trope here. Updates to the gun would be cool, since having to click for every shot is annoying when the damage output is so low compared to every other weapon in the game.

I'm curious to see how difficulty settings change the game. Admittedly we had fallen off a little due to everything feeling repetitive and easy, so I'm stoked to see what the new update brings!

Update as of the difficulty update 3/16: this game got a lot more challenging and I'm super into it.
reviews.developer_response: Thanks for the review. There will definitely be more characters and guns. And glad you tried the Hard mode!

LORT

Let me start off by saying the game is okay, good even. It's fun for a bit in the same way Risk of Rain 2 is, just going around and killing enemies with wacky abilities. If that's all you want in a game, then I'd recommend you buy it, its not that expensive and you'll get your fill and its fine.

However, I believe that there are very large problems with the game that make it not nearly as fun as a game like ROR2. First off, the items are mainly stat upgrades, there are some upgrades that do (sort of) cool stuff like a chance to shoot a ricocheting shot or dropping a mine when you dodge but for the most part I don't feel like the items are very interesting. Second, the enemies are not that interesting, they are sort of just fodder for you to murder and then get money and upgrades which is typical of these games. Third, The bosses are just not that interesting to me, they either die and never touch you or they stun lock you and you die immediately. Finally and my largest complaint, is the health, the bosses are huge damage sponges. The main difficulty in the game is how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ long it takes for the bosses to die. For example, the final boss has three real phases and one at the end that is a joke phase where he doesn't fight back. It took me like 30 seconds of just spamming my abilities to kill the joke phase where all he does is crawl around. It is not fun to attack an enemy that has little to no risk on your life for that long. The humor isn't my style and I never laughed at it but that's subjective so to each their own. I don't think this game is difficult it is just tedious.

With all that being said I'm sure the developers will fix some things and they are adding difficulty settings soon so maybe that will fix my issues with this game. As someone who has nearly 200 hours in ROR2, just play that if you want a game like this, it has much more polish and doesn't fall into the same traps as this game.
reviews.developer_response: We just released that difficulty update. You can check it out here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2956680/view/526495718648578185?

reviews.review:
(It appears the devs copy and pasted the same comment on any review that mentioned difficulty, and i've added the following paragraph in response to the comment and difficulty update they added)

So the developer response to people claiming there were difficulty scaling issues was to add a new difficulty - easy mode. I think this, at best, totally ignores the issue and, at worst, is a little dismissing. Most players are inclined to start games on a normal mode. This is especially true when normal difficulty is advertised as the "intended experience/difficulty" like it is in this game. No other changes were made to the scaling beyond adding an easy difficulty. As a matter of fact it appears they made normal difficulty slightly HARDER. I do not believe this addresses the complaints.

I want to make it clear that Lort is an objectively FINE game. But we live in the era of friendslop. There are so many games in this genre that are excellent and do everything Lort does but better.

First, let me get a personal gripe out. This game is ugly as hell. Its art style is that of a generic Unity asset flip. The characters are humorous but don't feel like they artistically belong in the same game. It feels like they were purchased on an asset store and modified. 

But that can be waived if the game is fun, so is it?

Well, sort of. My friends are fun. Playing games with my friends is fun. But playing most games with my friends is fun even if the games are bad. Lort focuses far more on the rogue-lite aspects than the friend-slop ones, and Lort is really skirting the line of being a fun rogue-lite. It's death by a thousand cuts. Little bad choices that build up frustration. 

Like when playing the archer, your crosshairs are centered on the screen which results in any enemies closer then mid range being obscured by your player model when placing your crosshair on them.

 Another example is the stat scaling. Weapons and player skills scale of str, dex, or int. But if you have a diverse party then everyone needs a different one, and most camps only give one of them. So it's often more optimal to split up from your friends and attack the camps that have your stat

There's also very little group play. There's not really any synergy between the classes. Most skills and weapons just do damage, the most synergy you can have is placing a debuff that increases damage on an enemy. The strict time limit on each map means that you're less likely to try to distribute loot to the best person, especially in large groups.

Enemies scale horrendously, being way too difficult starting on the second level without meta-progression upgrades that come far too slowly; It's also extremely unclear if these upgrades stack with your friend's upgrades. Enemies damage often one shots characters which spirals the run due to losing max health on going down. 

Melee characters don't have enough damage reduction to make up for being in melee, and the melee character is easily the worst character. Enemy attacks are often poorly telegraphed and there aren't enough dodge charges to feel good. 

So many little things that just hurt the game. But even if they were fixed I think Lort right now would only be an "Okay" game. There are much better friendslop games coming out right now, and much better rogue-likes, and much better games that do both. 

I think Lort has potential, and even could make a good night of fun. But it's too undercooked to be what it wants to be right now.

Lort looks and sounds amazing, but my 2 biggest gripes with this rougelike that doesn't make me want to play over & over again are as follows: 
1. Not enough items, both in terms of variety and acquiring them, which makes your build feel stale and underpowered AF 90% of the time. 
2. The end boss fight is so, so, so boring and goes on for way too long - this one really makes me never wanting to pick this game up again, I won't spoil it, but yeah not exciting. 

There's good potential here, but currently there's no real replay-ability imo.
reviews.developer_response: Thanks for the review. We will keep updating the game to add more variety and replayability, and improve the boss fights. Hope you can check it out again when we update it more!
